prerequisites: Basic knowledge about design & manufacturing process, structure and operation of machine components and assemblies, as well as principles of their selection and designing.
Well-grounded knowledge about basic manufacturing techniques and role of technological machines.
Ability to design a manufacturing process in the field of chipless forming and machining.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of engineering and operation principles of modern CNC manufacturing machines, in particular principles of their operation control.
Knowledge of selection principles of CNC manufacturing machines intended for specific machining tasks.
Knowledge of programming principles of CNC machines.
Ability to evaluate CNC manufacturing machines with respect to their suitability for specific machining tasks.
Ability to elaborate a program structure for basic CNC machines, as well as to use standard subprograms and cycles.
Ability to select and preset machining parameters, select tools and verify correctness of the developed programs.
Ability to search-out and use professional literature recommended for the course and to gain knowledge independently.
Ability to make use of modern IT tools.
Understanding of the necessity of systematic and individual work on mastering the course content.

syllabus_topics: General characteristics of manufacturing machines and their classification. Geometrical, kinematic and dynamic structures of the machines. Technical and operational parameters. Basic requirements.
Parts, mechanisms and components of CNC manufacturing machines: bodies, spindle and guiding assemblies, tooling and workpiece systems.
Main drive and feeding systems of modern manufacturing machines (basic requirements, exemplary solutions). Measurement, diagnostics and supervision systems.
Basics of automatic control of manufacturing machines. Classification of control systems (NC, CNC, DNC, AC and PLC systems).

Introduction to programming numerically controlled machines – geometrical basics of CNC control, coordinate systems, driver structure, interpolation. Ways of computer-aided programming – machining simulators.
Review of groups of CNC machines: lathes, milling machines, grinding machines (technical & usable features and purpose of the machines).
Review of groups of CNC machines: machining centres, autonomous machining stations (technical & usable features and purpose of the machines).
CNC machines for electrochemical and laser machining (technical & usable features and purpose of the machines).
Industrial robots and manipulators (structure, classification and application fields). Structure and purpose of coordinate measuring machines.
Multimachine, robotized manufacturing systems, production centres and lines (organizational structures and application fields). Computer-integrated manufacturing systems (CIM).
Machines and devices for additive manufacturing and reverse engineering techniques – exemplary applications.
Trends in development of CNC manufacturing machines (machines for HSC and HPC machining, hexapods, intelligent and hybrid machine tools).
Credit colloquium.
The use of the manipulator in processes of thermal spraying.
The use of robots in sheet and spot welding processes.
Control of machines in sheet metal forming processes.
The use of Coordinate Measuring Machine (CMM).
Automation of technological processes using PLC controllers (FESTO system).
Machines to implement additive technology (Rapid Prototyping).
Reverse Engineering equipment.
Crediting the course.
Selection of a machine tool, preparation of a workpiece, selection of tools and machining parameters.
Determination of characteristic points of a contour and location of a workpiece in the machine-tool workspace.
Elaboration of a driver software to control the manufacturing process on a CNC machine – linear and circular interpolation.
Elaboration of a driver software to control the manufacturing process on a CNC machine – establishing corrective functions; programming movements with correction of tool dimensions.
Elaboration of a driver software to control the manufacturing process on a CNC machine – subprograms technique, incremental programming, programming movements in a loop.
Elaboration of a driver software to control the manufacturing process on a CNC machine – use of machining cycles at programming.
Elaboration of a driver software to control the manufacturing process on a CNC machine – completion of the project and its verification.
Summary of the work – presentation of the project and its assessment.
teaching_methods: traditional lecture with the use of transparencies and slides
own work – preparation for crediting the lecture
self study - preparation for project class and laboratory
presentation of the project, crediting the lab subjects
assessment_rules: Lecture evaluation is based on a credit colloquium. Laboratory evaluation is based on a class admission test. Project evaluation is calculated as 0.5 * (Assessment of project preparation + Defence of the project).
